record.paper_title: Some open problems on the classical function space L1
record.context_brief: comparison of KSW-narrow and narrow operators
record.original_question: Is every KSW-narrow operator from L1[0,1] to an arbitrary Banach space X necessarily narrow in the earlier sense of narrow operators on L1?

evidence.quote: Problem 19. ([62]) Is every KSW-narrow operator from L1 to X narrow?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L_1=L_1[0,1]$ denote the Banach space of (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue integrable functions on $[0,1]$ with the usual norm. Recall the following two notions of "narrowness" for a bounded linear operator $T:L_1\to X$ into a Banach space $X$.

(i) (Narrow operator, Plichko–Popov sense.) $T$ is called narrow if for every measurable set $A\subseteq[0,1]$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a "sign" function $x:[0,1]\to\{-1,0,1\}$ supported on $A$ with $\int_0^1 x\,d\mu=0$ and $|x|=\mathbf{1}_A$ such that $\|T x\|<\varepsilon$.

(ii) (KSW-narrow operator, in the sense of Kadets–Shvydkoy–Werner.) $T$ is called KSW-narrow if for every non-empty relatively weakly open subset $U$ of the unit ball $B_{L_1}$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $u,v\in U$ with $\|T(u-v)\|<\varepsilon$ and $\|u-v\|>2-\varepsilon$ (equivalently, on every slice/relatively weakly open set one can find pairs that are nearly antipodal in $L_1$ but whose images under $T$ are nearly equal).

Question: Is it true that for every Banach space $X$, every KSW-narrow operator $T:L_1[0,1]\to X$ is narrow in the sense (i)?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turned up the general literature on narrow operators (Plichko–Popov, Kadets–Shvydkoy–Werner, Bilik–Kadets–Shvidkoy–Sirotkin–Werner) and on operators on $L_1$ with the Daugavet-type properties, but no source clearly announcing a resolution of the specific implication "KSW-narrow $\Rightarrow$ narrow" for operators from $L_1[0,1]$ into an arbitrary Banach space. The status therefore appears to remain unresolved in the literature surveyed, but this could not be definitively confirmed.

status_evidence.title: A lattice approach to narrow operators
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses several non-equivalent definitions of narrow operators on L1 and Köthe spaces and relations between them.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple competing definitions of 'narrow' coexist in the literature, and their precise interrelations on $L_1$ remain a subject of study.

status_evidence.title: Unconditionally convergent series of operators and narrow operators on L1
status_evidence.snippet: Studies properties of narrow operators on L1 with no statement equating the KSW notion with the classical narrow notion.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on narrow operators on $L_1$ does not record a resolution of the KSW-narrow vs. narrow question.

status_evidence.title: Narrow operators and the Daugavet property for ultraproducts
status_evidence.snippet: Kadets–Shvydkoy–Werner-style narrow operators are introduced via slices/weakly open sets in connection with the Daugavet property.
status_evidence.claim: The KSW notion of narrowness is the slice-based / Daugavet-related definition referenced in the problem.
